dialogue.text: Can you tell me exactly when the back pain started and what you were doing at that time?

I was at the gym doing deadlifts a few hours ago when I suddenly felt this sharp, shooting pain in my lower back. It happened right in the middle of my set - I had to stop immediately because the pain was so intense.
Does the pain shoot down into your leg, and if so, does it go past the knee? Any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your leg or foot?
Yes, the pain definitely shoots down the side of my leg and goes all the way into my foot. I haven't noticed any numbness or tingling, but the pain gets worse when I try to move or bend.
Have you noticed any weakness in your leg, difficulty lifting your foot, or any loss of bladder or bowel control?
No, I haven't had any weakness in my leg or trouble lifting my foot. And definitely no problems with bladder or bowel control - everything's normal in that regard.
Good, that's reassuring — no red flags there. Does coughing, sneezing, or straining make the pain worse?
Yes, actually! I noticed when I sneezed earlier, the pain shot down my leg even worse. It was really uncomfortable.
Does the pain feel worse when you're sitting versus standing or lying down, and have you tried anything that gives relief?

Sitting definitely makes it worse - I can barely sit down without the pain flaring up. Lying flat on my back seems to help a little bit, and I tried some ibuprofen which took the edge off but didn't make it go away completely.
Have you had any similar episodes of back pain before, or is this the first time this has happened?
This is the first time anything like this has ever happened to me. I've never had back pain like this before - it really caught me off guard.
Got it. One more thing — can you point to exactly where the pain is worst, and does it radiate more into your buttock, back of thigh, or side of your calf/foot?
The worst pain is right here in my lower back, and it radiates down the side of my leg - mostly along the outer part of my thigh and calf, and then into the top of my foot.

Given the sudden onset with a heavy lift, pain worse sitting and with sneezing, and radiation to the outer calf/top of foot — this points toward an L5 nerve root irritation from a disc herniation. Let's do a quick exam — REQUEST TEST: Straight_Leg_Raise_Test

- Range of Motion: Limited due to pain

**Neurological Examination:**

- Motor Function: No significant weakness noted
- Reflexes: Normal ankle and knee reflexes

**MRI Lumbar Spine:**
- Findings: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root
